An estimation of the $B^0_s\rightarrow K^+K^-$ decay time for $B^0_s$ mesons has been made with the help of around 37 picobarns of LHCb data from 2010. This measure allows for constraints on theories beyond the Standard Model that may influence the $B^0_s$ system and was found to be 1.442 picoseconds by employing two methods with varying degrees of uncertainty, specifically 0.096 (statistical) ± 0.008 (systematic) ± 0.003 (model-based).

This research paper focuses on the numerical solution of a stochastic control problem governed by a parabolic equation with the control variable affecting the diffusion coefficient, particularly with the presence of rough inputs; it establishes the convergence of a specific numerical discretization method and provides an alternative solution using a stochastic simulation technique known as the Monte-Carlo method.

Our analysis of data collected at the Pierre Auger Observatory from 2016 to 2018, spanning 640 days, of extensive cosmic ray air showers at energies above 8 EeV has revealed a notable anisotropy in the sky distribution. Specifically, we found an 18% variation in the cosmic ray flux aligned with the plane of the Milky Way, which is statistically significant at 3.2 standard deviations. This anomaly is not present in data collected at lower energies, specifically 8 EeV to 56 EeV, indicating that the propagation of the highest energy cosmic rays is affected by the magnetic fields in the intergalactic space. Furthermore, the air shower data exhibits a slight preference towards the direction of the Galactic Center, although this is not statistically significant. To further investigate the observed features, we employed Monte Carlo simulations of the large area air shower detector data and compared the results with the distribution of distant active galactic nuclei. The comparison indicates a marginal increase in the likelihood of preferring the direction of AGN, with a likelihood ratio of 1.4 and a corresponding p-value of 0.12.

The ATLAS detector at the LHC gathered p+Pb data with a centre-of-mass energy of 5.02 TeV and 25 nb$^{-1}$, enabling a measurement of the nuclear modification factor for charged particles across a wide transverse momentum spectrum, from 0.2 to 100.0 GeV/c. This study also accounts for various sources of systematic uncertainty, including a geometric acceptance effect spanning 2.0 to 100.0 GeV/c.

Quantum mechanics can be explored on noncommutative spaces, which are defined by specific relations that introduce a set of functions that are first-order polynomial in momenta. These functions possess unique properties, such as being compatible with themselves and commutative with the position operators. By parameterizing the space using a set of constants, including a deformation parameter, the trivial star product is obtained. This leads to the derivation of a unitary equivalent noncommutative version, which is the Moyal-like star product. This new product is then used to formulate quantum mechanics, where the Hamiltonian is given in terms of operators. The dynamics can be analyzed using the Heisenberg equations of motion, and a mapping is established between noncommutative and commutative mechanics. This mapping allows for the study of various Hamiltonians, such as the free particle, and reveals relationships between their trajectories. Additionally, the relationship between the noncommutative and commutative formulations can be expressed in matrix form.

In evaluating the potential of federated learning, we tested its performance in training deep learning models to analyze digital pathology images, models that could then be developed through a non-invasive process using data from multiple hospitals, and compared this approach to a traditional data aggregation method. Our research, presented at the 2020 Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition, revealed the effectiveness of federated learning in these complex image analyses.

In this study, a high-speed optical transmission system is demonstrated, achieving 80 Gbit/s PDM-QPSI signal transmission over 100 km of dispersion-affected submarine cable. To achieve this, we utilized an 80 Gbit/s electrical signal generation technique, combined with a low-speed electrical equalization technique to compensate for the chromatic dispersion. As a result, our experiment successfully showed the feasibility of high-speed optical data transmission over older, cost-effective G.655 type submarine cables.

Deep Learning models like Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCNs) hold great promise for handling time-series data. TCNs leverage a technique called time-dilated convolution to capture long-term dependencies in tasks such as speech recognition and video classification. By multiplying the conventional convolution with a time-dilation factor, dependent on the layer number, TCNs can efficiently model long-range temporal patterns. This innovative approach allows TCNs to replace cyclic buffers and make predictions directly from raw inputs, eliminating the need for complex feature extraction and temporal aggregation. We've applied TCNs to a diverse range of tasks including speech recognition, video classification, and time-series forecasting, using raw inputs and achieving state-of-the-art results on several benchmark datasets. Our results show that TCNs can outperform leading baselines such as C3D and ConvLSTM in video classification, using significantly fewer parameters. We've also released our code and models to facilitate further research in this area.
This paper proves that any finite-dimensional Zinbiel algebra over a given field possesses a specific characteristic - nilpotency, building on a previous discovery that these algebras are solvable.

This study presents new findings on the behavior of particles produced in LHC heavy-ion collisions, specifically looking at how the angle and magnitude of the particles' momentum vary in different directions perpendicular to the particles' spin. Using data from 7 TeV lead-lead collisions, we found that the fluctuations in the angle of the particles' momentum follow a normal distribution, with the amount of fluctuation being 0.12 radians. This value of about 7 degrees is significant and may help us better understand the complex behavior of quark-gluon plasma. Furthermore, we observed that the fluctuations in the magnitude of the particles' momentum vary at a rate of about 0.15 times the average momentum squared, which is a new discovery and provides insight into the movement of the plasma itself.

The unified correspondence theory initially lacked a robust algebraic foundation. We have developed the unified correspondence framework within a algebraic setting for certain classes of complex algebras, extending beyond standard complex algebras. This framework is called expansively generated complex algebras. Our expansion has the capacity to preserve the unified correspondence principles, allowing us to derive specific correspondences for modal algebras and relation algebras as applications.

This research focuses on dealing with inconsistencies in data tables that contain missing values. Most current methods for resolving inconsistencies are iterative, which means they continue to search for solutions as long as the quality of the data improves in each step. This becomes a problem in the early stages when the table has many inconsistencies, because these methods rely on assumptions that may not hold true regarding the relationships between data values. Our novel approach treats inconsistencies in data tables from a logical perspective, viewing them as violations of certain rules, and defining preferences based on the strength of those rules. This approach allows us to drop assumptions that are commonly made in current methods and develop a new, rigorous way of evaluating data quality. As a result, incomplete data values are seen as having infinite potential and cannot be assigned a specific data type. This, in turn, leads to a new set of queries that cannot be answered by traditional approaches, and instead require a combination of data types and uncertainty representations. Our method also offers a new way of answering such queries by combining those data types and uncertainty representations.

This paper presents a novel dynamic econometric model called Time-Varying Poisson AutoRegressive with external covariates, specifically designed to analyze and forecast count-based time series data. Our research demonstrates the efficiency of TVPARX in capturing complex patterns within such data, including seasonal trends, making it a valuable alternative to existing methods. To evaluate its performance, we used real-world datasets across various fields, as well as count-based artificial data, and the results showed TVPARX to be a highly effective and versatile forecasting tool.

We introduce Neural Descriptor Fields (NDFs), a novel object representation that
integrates continuous object and rigid scene transformations within the context
of six-dimensional object manipulation tasks. Our framework ensures object
descriptions remain consistent under combined rotations and translations,
facilitating seamless interaction with diverse robotic systems. Leveraging the
continuous nature of our description, the robot can effortlessly infer how
reorienting an object in its environment affects its relationship to that object.
We validate our approach through real-world robotic manipulation experiments on
actual objects, demonstrating the efficacy of NDFs in facilitating consistent
object manipulation under object and rigid transformations.

The SiD Detector is one of the two proposed final detectors that will be used at the International Linear Collider, alongside the ILD Detector. The SiD combines the best aspects of the existing TPC designs, such as the CMS and ATLC, to achieve excellent momentum resolution in particles. It achieves this through the use of a large, high-resolution Time Projection Chamber with an inner vertexing system, situated within a powerful superconducting magnet. The detector maintains full hermeticity and 4-$\pi$ coverage while also being capable of distinguishing between different types of particles through advanced TPC and vertexing systems. It has full flavor sensitivity, allowing it to differentiate between different types of particles, and includes a low-background final focus system that allows it to identify the Higgs boson in diphoton decays. The SiD design also has full flavor sensitivity, allowing it to differentiate between different types of particles, and includes a low-background final focus system that allows it to identify the Higgs boson in diphoton decays.

We have conducted an in-depth analysis of the globular cluster Tononzintla 2, also known as NGC 2808, utilizing a comprehensive dataset of 1218 stars. This cluster is unique in its multi-population structure, which poses a significant challenge for astronomers studying the evolution of early universe populations. By analyzing the cluster's color-magnitude diagram, we identified distinct populations and investigated their characteristics. Our analysis focused on identifying the metallicity of each population and its corresponding age. We also examined the helium content of the second population and its potential formation through primordial or self-enriched processes. Our findings suggest that this population has a metallicity of +0.15 dex, a helium content of 0.23-0.28, and an age of approximately 10 billion years. These characteristics indicate that it is highly probable that this population was formed through self-enriched processes, thus providing valuable insights into the formation and evolution of multi-population globular clusters.

The Isabelle Archive of Formal Proofs has amassed substantial size over recent years, presenting difficulties in discovering and comprehending the available content. To address this challenge, the Archiver project was initiated to create an organized, searchable presentation of the Archive. This pertainential system is designed to present and combine proofs in a modular fashion, allowing users to interactively visualize the material at hand while maintaining a degree of independence from the underlying Isabelle/PP structure.

Using the functional renormalization group, we have determined the first non-universal correction to the critical radius of an interface in O(N) universality classes. For a specific case with N=2, we have found the critical radius's minimum value at long wavelengths. The first non-universal correction's magnitude at this minimum is found to be approximately 0.224 R_∞. With a newly developed method, which involves matching the results of the RG with those of the renormalized field theory, we have verified the value of the minimum radius for a specific case with a fixed spin, finding agreement to 5%. Additionally, we have found that for N values slightly greater than 2, the minimum radius's value is discontinuous with the Gaussian fixed point value, which is approximately 1.149 R_∞.

In statistics and machine learning, it is frequently observed that optimization gradients offer valuable information, yet their effectiveness relies heavily on a favorable landscape structure. We develop a general framework to analyze non-convex optimization landscapes through the concept of local convexity, and we specifically apply this framework to estimators of stochastic matrices in a matrix completion setting. Our framework allows for the assessment of local convexity properties, and as a result, we can determine specific rates of local strong convexity and smoothness, and identify conditions under which the global minimum is unique. The derived rates of local convexity match the rates of convergence of certain optimization estimators to the optimal rank-one matrix, and we demonstrate the applicability of our results to various types of symmetric matrices, including binary matrices, sign matrices, and random projection matrices.

Modern metasurfaces are highly functional interfaces between space and matter, 
characterized by unique optical properties resulting in significant potential 
across multiple technological fields. Due to the intricate nature of metasurfaces, 
they pose challenges in visualization and analysis, which can be complicated by 
the varying scales present in geometry, illumination, and observation. To facilitate 
understanding and exploration of metasurfaces, we introduce a novel framework 
called metasurface zosoms, which provides an illuminated cross-sectional view of the 
structure at the present scale. These zosoms not only aid in visualizing and 
interpreling optical phenomena but also serve as valuable tools for representing 
metasurfaces in 3D, modeling light interactions in enclosed spaces, and guiding 
experimental setups. The concepts presented in this paper are demonstrated through 
multiple case studies involving diverse metasurfaces and light interactions.

The primary objective of this research is to validate the smooth local orbital linearization theorem for smooth vector fields with a full set of nearby first integrals, especially those at nondegenerate singular points. This theoretical validation relies heavily on key concepts, including the formal orbital linearization theorem for formally integrable vector fields, the application of the blow-up technique, and the application of the Sternberg-Chen theorem.

This report outlines a deep learning approach known as the Electron Correlation
Potential Neural Network (eCPNN), which can learn simplified potential functions
that accurately capture the intricate instantaneous relationships among electrons
within complex atomic systems. Trained in an unsupervised manner with constrained
data derived from Full Configuration Interaction one-electron density functions, the
eCPNN model effectively predicts total atomic energies with remarkable precision.

We have identified a massive structure, dubbed the Giant Arc, which spans approximately 300 megaparsecs and lies directly behind the Shapley Supercluster. This 14 billion light-year away arc consists of multiple clusters and great arcs of galaxy groups that collectively hold around 100 million times the mass of our Sun. We estimate a 2% probability of such a massive structure forming a chance alignment in front of the supercluster. The Giant Arc's existence challenges the $\Lambda$CDM model of cosmology, which predicts fewer instances of such massive structures at such great distances. Further research is needed to confirm our initial findings.

A new method of analyzing data from ground-based photometry systems has been developed to accurately measure the optical depth of aerosols in the atmosphere. By using a specific dataset from the HAPI camera system, a conventional statistical approach was used to obtain an estimate of the optical depth with a smaller margin of error. To achieve this, a new variable was created to account for the influence of sunlight intensity and data points outside the range of the HAPI camera. This method was successful in reducing uncertainty associated with measurements taken during varying weather conditions. The analysis also revealed the impact of various factors such as system noise and data quality on the measurement's accuracy. The study highlights the importance of using a high-quality dataset and performing multiple measurements under stable atmospheric conditions to minimize errors. The proposed analysis method can be applied to datasets from other photometry systems and may serve as a useful tool for researchers studying the effects of the atmosphere on the Earth's climate.

Recently, estimating a 6D object pose using convolutional neural networks has seen significant progress. Current research primarily focuses on specific methodological approaches rather than exploring the broader spectrum of 2D-based and 3D-based techniques. Most studies utilize synthetic images and do not compare results on real images. This study provides a comprehensive review and discussion on current 6D pose estimation methods, emphasizing their practical applications. We examine representative approaches from 2D and 3D methods, discuss their strengths and weaknesses, and suggest potential future research directions.

Peridynamic theories have seen a significant amount of research in recent years due to their ability to model complex material failures without the need for complex algorithms. Bond-based Peridynamics, a particular approach, has been effective in doing so, but it has certain limitations that can be addressed through alternative methods, such as the proposed implicit integrator. This new method combines time integration and material failure processes into a single implicit scheme, which can be solved using a variant of the Newton method. By formulating the solution in an extended phase space, this approach ensures a more stable and accurate solution, even in cases where traditional explicit methods struggle. Numerical tests demonstrate the superiority of this new approach over standard explicit methods, including their second-order counterparts.

We present GGLasso, a Python-based library that provides a comprehensive set of tools for working with Generalised Graphical Lasso models across multiple views and partial covariance targets. The PALS and PXLS approaches are fully implemented in GGLasso for working with partIAL Least Squares and graphically modelled covariance matrices.

Numerous numerical methods for solving partial differential equations in molecular dynamics simulations, such as configurational averaging, normal mode analysis, and the use of harmonic oscillators networks, have proven highly accurate in biomolecule simulations. These methods share key advantages: they are deterministic, allow for seamless integration of classical and quantum mechanical forces, and maintain high computational efficiency due to the absence of random number generation and the linearity of the involved calculations. Building upon a recent study, we have derived the exact mathematical relationship between the average positions and variances of quantum mechanical masses and their classical counterparts within the harmonic oscillator network model, thereby laying the foundation for developing a more rigorous mixed classical-quantum harmonic oscillator network method.

Numerical relativity simulations of mergers between black holes have shown that dark matter with a minimum mass of about 10 solar masses can form massive, stable orbits around the point masses of the black holes.  These orbits can eventually lead to a merger, but this timescale is often longer than the age of the universe.  However, for lower mass dark matter, whose de Broglie wavelength is on the order of a millimeter, the effects of quantum pressure and interference prevent the formation of stable orbits.  As a result, a large amplitude wave pattern emerges in the gravitational waves during the merger of binaries with equal mass black holes.  In contrast, binaries with a mass ratio of 100 show little to no such wave effects, as the heavier mass dark matter forms stable orbits around the lighter mass black hole.  These findings have important implications for the study of binaries consisting of dark matter and black holes, as well as the potential for using gravitational waves to constrain the properties of dark matter.

We investigate the long-term behavior of a stretched Euler-Bernoulli beam on a star-shaped metric graph with rigid boundary conditions, and prove its exponential stability. To achieve this, we first establish a variational formulation and derive sufficient conditions for exponential stability based on the type of damping applied. By leveraging recent results, we can demonstrate that the eigenvectors associated with this formation are analytically smooth along the graph's arms, enabling direct comparison with damping mechanisms at the central vertex.

Researchers utilized acoustic lenses composed of PMMA to study dark matter axions using the HAYSTAC experiment. Although PMMA functions effectively as an acoustic lens, it can produce waste heat when axions are converted to photons. As a result, the temperature of the lens can increase significantly, altering its acoustic properties and reducing the efficiency of the acousto-electric conversion. In an effort to address this issue, we investigated Stycast 1090SI as a viable alternative to PMMA. Through a combination of measurements and theoretical calculations, we found that Stycast 1090SI generates approximately 1000 times less waste heat than PMMA. Additionally, it offers an advantageous combination of acoustic impedance and mechanical quality factor. To verify the practicality of this material, we fabricated and tested Stycast acoustic lenses in the  GHz frequency range. The lenses demonstrated effective sound wave focusing capabilities. The lens with the optimal design exhibited a combination of impedance and quality factor that is comparable to PMMA. These findings suggest that Stycast 1090SI is an excellent candidate for use in future axion detection experiments.

Our new method calculates a variation of eigenvector centrality for multi-layered networks that incorporate node importance across different layers. In these networks, defined by separate interconnected graphs without connections between different layers, the value of a node's centrality depends on its connections within each layer, as well as its connections in other layers that influence its own centrality value. By utilizing a matrix-based approach, we developed an efficient calculation process that reduces the complexity to O(km^n) operations, where m is the total number of nodes across all layers, and the number of operations scales linearly with the number of layers when the average connections per node remain similar. Comparison with conventional methods shows our approach's significant advantage in processing large-scale multi-layer networks.

We tackle the issue of non-blind deblurring and demosaicking on noisy raw images with blur, addressed by designing a joint deblurring and demosaicking network that takes a raw image and a depth map as inputs. To handle the varying quality of motion blur, we employ an adaptive module that adjusts the strength of the filtering effect. Additionally, a dual-path architecture is used to efficiently remove both the mosaic pattern and the image noise. The proposed network is trained on a large dataset of synthetic raw images with varying levels of blur and noise, and its performance is evaluated on a real-world dataset, demonstrating its ability to produce high-quality demosaicked and deblurred images.

Recently, we generated the $R$-Poincar\'e algebra using deformed brackets that adhered to the principle of naturalness and were idempotent to first order. These structures were classified up to the fourth order in a recent study. In this paper, we show that the spacetime defined by the $R$-Poincar\'e algebra can be redefined as de Sitter spacetime. This transformation is possible because the Minkowski metric can be viewed as a Taylor series expansion of the de Sitter metric with a zero cosmological constant as its first term. Consequently, the $R$-Minkowski spacetime is essentially a deformed version of de Sitter spacetime, not the AdS spacetime commonly associated with the Poincar\'e algebra.

This study introduces an open source Python framework that utilizes background knowledge and observational data for the purpose of inferring causal relationships. This framework is comprised of the 'cdt' package, which executes a comprehensive causal discovery process to identify the causal interactions and the causal network structure among the variables of interest. The 'cdt' package is designed to integrate several existing methods for causal discovery, including SCM learning, CSP learning, metric-based algorithms, and exact causal structure learning algorithms. The framework is built upon the Python programming language and relies on established packages such as NetworkX, DGL, and scikit-learn. It is suitable for application in a diverse range of scenarios, including the modeling of technical systems, biological pathways, and economic market dynamics. The source code for the 'cdt' framework is publicly available on GitHub.

This study investigates the surface seal that occurs during a sphere's impact with a water surface, where the point of contact is blocked by a pressure field, causing a net force that opposes the motion of the impacting object. Through high-speed imaging and optical measurements, we examine seal formation in three-dimensional space using painted glass spheres that shatter upon contact with water, allowing for a detailed observation of internal pressure distributions. The data collected reveals the occurrence and characteristics of the surface seal in space and time for a wide range of impact speeds, specifically between 0.5 and 3 meters per second, and sphere sizes spanning from 1.25 to 5 centimeters. The results show that smaller spheres and those with higher impact speeds are more susceptible to the formation of the surface seal. The findings indicate that the surface seal begins to develop when the dimensionless impact speed exceeds a threshold value of approximately 0.2 and becomes negligible when the impact speed surpasses another threshold value of approximately 1.2. Moreover, the speed at which the fluid fills the space between the sphere and its shadow on the polar axis is found to be directly proportional to the impact speed, specifically with an exponent of approximately 0.7.

A recent study by Eichhorn, Melville, and Rastogi has uncovered how certain gravity theories, specifically new modifications to Einstein's general relativity, can emerge from fundamental principles applied to higher-spin gravity. This paper deepens that investigation by examining the role of global symmetries in these gravities and exploring whether any of their charges or associated symmetries remain conserved. We find that in cases where a global symmetry involves a U(1) component, effective theta-term contributions can be added to the gravities' spacetime symmetry transformations. Furthermore, we demonstrate through a numerical approach that in a particular quarter-BPS vacuum, both the charges of this global symmetry and spacetime itself behave in accordance with Einstein's general relatory principles. However, when considering more complex global symmetries, we discover that their charges cannot be effectively represented. By analyzing the relationship between global symmetries and gauge symmetries, we also identify constraints on which global symmetries can coexist with massive higher-spin fields within a specific holographic context known as the ABJM model.

Mobile devices are increasingly incorporating multiple hardware areas to broaden their capabilities and improve security for sensitive applications. This trend suggests a future where the various hardware areas collaborate and interact, presenting an opportunity to move critical applications from isolated areas to interconnected systems. To facilitate this, we developed a method for creating applications using a dedicated secure hardware area that collaborates with the main operating system. Our approach involves a custom secure application framework and a novel resource allocation system that operates across the device's CPU. A key feature of this system is its dynamic adjustment of the application's memory space based on the current context, which enhances performance and security. To validate our method, we built a multi-domain design for a smartphone and conducted a series of experiments and security tests. The results demonstrate significant performance improvements up to 2.5 times, as well as the ability to prevent malicious attacks.

We investigate the impact of intentional or accidental data sabotage on reinforcement learning systems, specifically focusing on a particular scenario where the environment's reward function is manipulated to some degree. Even in this situation, we have discovered that the NPG algorithm can learn an almost optimal policy, achieving up to $O(n^{-1/2})$ optimality, where $n$ represents the number of gradient updates required to establish a nearly optimal policy. Notably, this finding holds true when the environment is not stochastic, and it is robust to the manipulation as long as the maximum level of corruption does not exceed 0.5. To accomplish this, we have developed a novel technique to track value functions with bounded corruption and used it to prove the convergence of NPG under these conditions.

We uncover an unselectable version of the box game paradox, featuring players making remarkably accurate predictions of unknown real numbers without access to relevant information. Additionally, our analysis confirms the requirement of choice in solving the classic problem and examines alternative configurations of the game.

Our calculations using first-principles methods reveal that cubanite exhibits unusual orbital selectivity, with electrons occupying certain molecular orbitals while being localized in other atomic ones. This phenomenon is exceptionally rare in 3d transition metal compounds, providing a theoretical basis for the experimentally observed lack of charge disproportionation, anomalous Mössbauer spectra, and ferromagnetic coupling between adjacent iron ions.

A promising avenue in quantum physics research involves utilizing dark excitons in semiconductor quantum dots as a source of entangled photons. These dark excitons can emit more rapidly than their bright counterparts and do not suffer from quantum decoherence. However, since dark excitons do not interact with light directly, their formation must be induced through optical means. We have developed a novel technique to optically create dark excitons in semiconductor quantum dots through continuous excitation at low temperatures. This process consistently produces a signature of dark excitons that is less affected by technical fluctuations and can be reliably created without relying on complex multi-photon processes. Our new approach provides a straightforward pathway to produce dark excitons and quantum states of dark excitons for the purpose of generating entangled photons.

Researchers have discovered a class of chiral honeycomb lattices that possess a chiral spin configuration. This configuration results in the formation of stable Dirac cones in the bands of this two-dimensional electronic lattice. The research demonstrates that impurities within the lattice have the ability to open a gap in the Dirac cones while maintaining robustness. The researchers have identified a mechanism to control the spin of carriers in two-dimensional devices made from the material MB8CH, thereby enabling the realization of stable conducting regions in the bands. The properties of these lattices and the mechanisms behind GBC and spin-gated devices are also explored in detail through the use of first-principles calculations.

Using the single quantum catalysis technique, we explore the characteristics of a specific type of light known as SPCCSs. By analyzing appropriate metrics, we find that SPCCSs exhibit notable sub-Poissonian and quantum interference patterns. Furthermore, the Minkowski and Wigner functions demonstrate distinct quantum behavior in SPCCSs. Notably, these light states possess enhanced quantum features compared to another type of light, the Jayaldharan's coherent states (JCSs). Additionally, SPCCSs show macroscopic quantum superposition properties due to the presence of a highly excited quantum state induced by a single catalytic photon.

In General Relativity using the Newman-Penrose formalism, the use of bivectors plays a key role in identifying the precise solutions to Einstein's field equations. This review focuses on explaining the fundamental principles and detailed calculations of bivectors within the Newman-Penrose formalism, specifically in its original form. Furthermore, it examines the application of this concept to classify solutions into the six types defined by the Newman-Penrose algorithm.

A recent framework has been developed to integrate artificial neural networks into the rational design of molecules, specifically the OPM4 framework. This framework enables the exploration of a molecule's property distribution in a chemical sub-space, guided by a artificial neural network. This tool facilitates the visualization of property distributions in 2D and 3D molecular spaces, facilitating a more efficient and efficient molecule design process. As an example, we illustrate the application of this tool in the molecule design of compounds with specific electronic characteristics and compounds with specific reactivity and stability properties. Furthermore, we introduce a novel evaluation metric for rationally designed molecules, comparing their experimental and predicted properties. This evaluation metric assesses the accuracy of designed molecules in meeting their target properties and comparing their structural similarity to reference molecules.

This research focuses on a class of continuous time dynamic optimization problems, which can be challenging to address due to the absence of analytical solutions. Our goal is to showcase how optimal control problems without closed-form solutions can be tackled using an indirect method. We utilize Pontryagin's maximum principle to derive necessary conditions for optimality and employ the continuous Galerkin finite element method to discretize the resulting first-order equations. This approach allows us to efficiently solve the optimization problem using standard numerical techniques. By applying our methodology to two problem examples, we demonstrate its effectiveness and convergence properties.

Identifying tumors in the esophagus from CT scans is a challenging task, as manual delineation is time-consuming and prone to variability. This study presents a deep learning-based approach, utilizing a 3D U-Net architecture, to automate and improve the segmentation of esophageal tumors. By training and validating the model on a dataset of 120 CT scans, annotated by medical experts, it demonstrated significant accuracy, with a Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of 0.84 and a Hausdorff Distance of 10.13mm. This method outperformed alternative approaches, including thresholding and distance transformation, and its ability to handle complex tumor geometries marks a step forward in radiology.

Our novel approach to an ill-defined geosteering problem involves formulating a
convex optimization problem that can be solved efficiently in real-time. In this
framework, we design a convex approximation of the objective function and
constraints, taking into account the available well log measurements and flow
regulation constraints. By utilizing online optimization techniques, we are able to
guarantee a certain level of closeness to the optimal reservoir trajectory. To test
our method, we apply it to a 2D model of an offshore well and demonstrate its
effectiveness in achieving log concentration and avoiding a target sandstone layer.

Named entity recognition (NER) is a fundamental task in natural language processing (NLP) that serves as a basis for many NLP applications. One notable NER challenge is the nested named entity problem, which arises when named entities contain other named entities. In this paper, we present a novel bidirectional LSTM-based neural network architecture that can parse both sequential and non-sequential named entities within a nested structure. Our proposed model utilizes a holistic nested structure to model the relationships between named entities and their components. To train the model, a nested NER dataset is created and used. The experiment results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed model in achieving high NER accuracy.

We extend the tropical enumeration of bitangents to a specific class of curves defined by an irreducible equation in parameterized form. For this equation, we demonstrate that the number of tropical bitangents with finite flatness matches a specific configuration of points on a curve, thereby yielding computation formulas for both enumeration and localized values.

Research into the location detection of mobile nodes within wireless sensor networks is currently ongoing. We develop and test an innovative RSSI-based location finding method suitable for 802.15.4 (ZigBee) networks. To counteract interference between different technologies operating in the same frequency range, we design and execute a new method for calculating the distance between nodes. The aim of this approach is to minimize the average error in location estimation, and when compared to ideal conditions, we have found that it can achieve nearly the same level of accuracy. To further enhance performance in real-world conditions, we make several local improvements to the method, and these changes significantly reduce error at both short and long range.

Multilingualism is a well-documented phenomenon in which individuals seamlessly blend two or more languages, a practice referred to as code-mixing or code-switching. This behavior is driven by a variety of factors, including personal, social, and psychological motivations, and is widely embraced and celebrated in many communities around the world. Despite its prevalence, research on code-mixing has yielded limited insights into the underlying mechanisms that guide its occurrence, and current models of bilingualism and multilingualism fail to adequately account for the active choice to mix languages. To address this gap, a computational model called the Multilingual Dynamic Switching Architecture has been developed, incorporating the concept of code-mixing and enabling multilingual agents to draw from multiple linguistic systems in a single utterance. Through extensive simulations, this model has demonstrated the ability to learn to use different languages based on contextual cues and produce novel patterns of code-mixing behavior.

Human-generated descriptions are commonly used to train and evaluate image description systems, which are typically ranked based on their similarity to these descriptions. This method's reliability hinges on the quality of these descriptions. Since, as demonstrated in Section 2, current datasets are inadequate, I believe we require more precise guidelines balancing visual, linguistic, and domain expertise to create high-quality reference data. We also discuss the impact of ranking metrics and propose future research directions for improving image description systems.

Tantalum oxides ($Ta_2O_5$) have emerged as promising alternatives to traditional high-Z materials in hadrontherapy, due to their lower atomic number and tunable properties. To gain a deeper understanding of the electronic and structural characteristics of $Ta_2O_5$, extensive simulations were performed to explore the effects of varying the stoichiometry, lattice constants, and oxidation states. The results revealed the existence of stable phases within a specific range of oxygen-to-tantalum ratios, and the effects of changing the lattice constants were found to primarily affect the band gap rather than the overall electronic structure. The research also indicated that the phase with the largest band gap occurs at a specific oxygen-to-tantalum ratio, and the effects of photon and neutron irradiation were found to affect the band gap in a similar way to the effects of changing the lattice constants. The implications of these findings for the use of $Ta_2O_5$ in hadrontherapy are discussed.

Previous studies have linked misinformation to online community polarization. 
However, little is known about its dissemination within smaller groups or individual 
social networks. We investigated how the geographic distribution of a person's 
friends on Twitter influences news and information spread. By analyzing 7.5 
million users and 35.5 million follow relationships from the Google 
Personality Forum dataset, we found that a person's Big Five personality 
trait scores can predict the circulation of news, including fake news, up 
to 9% as much as their political ideology. Specifically, individuals with 
higher levels of openness, conscientiousness, and agreeableness tend to have 
more followers who follow the same news as they do. In contrast, individuals 
with higher neuroticism or lower extraversion tend to follow more breaking 
news but see less of it shared by their followers. These patterns vary across 
different political environments, with individuals in red states showing 
different follower effects compared to their blue state counterparts.

Detecting suspicious activities in real-time data streams is crucial for secure systems. Traditional detection methods, which rely on rule-based algorithms, often generate high false positive rates. Machine learning-based detections can be more accurate but require extensive labeled data for training. This study explores the use of semi-supervised algorithms to detect anomalies in real-time streaming data using a limited amount of labeled data. To achieve this, we developed a novel semi-supervised stream learning algorithm called SS3Learn. Our algorithm combines a light-weight stream learning algorithm with a data condensation algorithm to efficiently manage the limited amount of labeled data. Experimental evaluations on multiple datasets demonstrate that SS3Learn effectively detects suspicious activities with a high accuracy rate while minimizing the amount of data required for training.

Humans employ spoken language to efficiently convey complex tasks to others through the use of spatially referenced descriptions. Many robots have been trained by observing human actions without receiving verbal feedback from their instructors. Our research aims to investigate whether spoken instructions can be utilized to process raw audio from humans demonstrating tasks to the robot via demonstration. We compiled a new dataset called AudioInstruct consisting of 100 short voice instructions from humans who also recorded their own commands while demonstrating five everyday household tasks to the robot. We developed and tested multiple baseline models to process the raw audio data. Our findings revealed that some features, such as MFCC and prosody, were crucial in capturing the meaning of the spoken instructions. A simple baseline model outperformed other more complex alternatives.

Building on previous work, we propose an algorithm to randomly generate ordered trees of any degree, based on a pre-specified sequence of numbers representing possible node connections. Our method allows for the generation of binary, n-ary trees, or those with limited connection restrictions using a corresponding sequence. It uses the sequence to fill a larger predefined sequence, effectively removing the need to know the total number of tree nodes in advance. It's worth noting that previous methods could only handle trees with binary or n-ary structures. We offer the algorithm's analysis, demonstrating its linear-time efficiency and uniform distribution accuracy, and provide implementation code in C++.

Quantum field theory complexity, both of states and operators, presents significant challenges in research and PAINC. To address these challenges, we investigate the complexity of states and operators within the framework of conformal field theories in 1+1 dimensions, utilizing the universal circuit complexity definition. Leveraging the powerful tool of symmetry breaking networks, we calculate the operator complexity of primary fields in the TCFT, and subsequently, the complexity of coherent states in the CFT by operating a simple field polynomial on the vacuum state. Moreover, we also examine the complexity of multi-particle states and fields composed of multiple primary fields.

Conversational interfaces, which utilize agents engaged in dialogue with users, have been developed to improve the experience of interacting with complex systems and services. The advancement of deep learning has led to the creation of sophisticated conversational agents capable of handling intricate tasks. However, these agents often lack genuine understanding and the capacity for critical thinking, which can be triggered by emotional stimuli in real-life situations. This paper provides an overview of integrating affect into artificial intelligence-driven conversational agents, exploring key theories, computational methods, and practical applications. The material can serve as a foundation for further research in this evolving field.

Using a sophisticated statistical approach, this study calculates uncertainty ranges for various mass measurements, based on a established framework. This method is then applied to calculate uncertainty for measuring a hypothetical 'Planet X', located beyond our known solar system bodies, at different distances from the sun, using current and future solar system measurements with SKA and CMB-S4, which could potentially reveal signs of 'Planet X's gravitational influence through the movement of the solar system's center of mass relative to the cosmic microwave background. It is discovered that with current technology, uncertainty estimates for 'Planet X' at 400 AU begin at roughly 12 times larger than expected, increasing to more than 100 times larger at 10,000 AU, which highlights the importance of more precise future measurements with SKA and CMB-S4 to reduce uncertainty to roughly 30 times larger than expected at 10,000 AU, while also providing an opportunity to refine our understanding of the solar system's mass measurements and potentially uncover a distant 'Planet X'.

Previous studies have demonstrated that Translation Memory (TM) can enhance Neural Machine Translation (NMT) performance, yet TM requires parallel data which can be costly to acquire. It has been reported that monolingual data in TM can provide benefits to NMT, but the underlying mechanisms were unclear. This research investigates monolingual data's impact on NMT, specifically investigating how it influences the ability to recover source information from TM-compressed representations. Our experiments reveal that TM pretraining generally hinders NMT's capacity to recover source information, an effect exacerbated by larger increases in sentence complexity. Conversely, we discover that this adverse effect can be mitigated when TM contains errors sourced from high-quality parallel data, resulting in nomenclature learning abilities comparable to baseline NMT models. Furthermore, we investigate nomenclature learning in deeper contexts and observe a recovery of source information, leading to improved nomenclature learning abilities. These findings offer valuable insights into TM's influence on NMT and suggest potential directions for future work.

Researchers have proposed that specific patterns in the Cosmic Microwave Background, namely low-variance circles and Hawking points, could provide evidence for the Conformal Cyclic Cosmology (CCC) theory, which suggests the existence of multiple universes. To investigate the validity of this theory, a study analyzed the impact of cold spots on the creation of Hawking points in a next-generation universe. Utilizing the CCC framework, a simulation was conducted to model this process, and the characteristics of the resulting Hawking points were compared to data from the Planck satellite. Although one simulation pattern matched the observations, it was determined that the presence of a large cold spot, such as the one located at l=214, would leave a distinct imprint on the CMB and could be classified as a Hawking point itself, contradicting the explanation of the so-called 'Cold Flow' in Rottach and Schwarz's analysis.

This paper builds upon previous work of the second author with Daskalopoulos and Vazquez, which involved introducing a Yamabe flow based on fractional curvature and demonstrating the existence of mild solutions. The current research expands on that study by establishing the convergence of the flow under certain data conditions within a broader framework. The new results are derived from an approach simplified by Struwe in his book.

To recognize new categories with limited labeled data, few-shot learning aims
to efficiently classify new concepts. This study investigates the performance of
three optimization methods in comparative experiments on the few-shot learning
task using the miniImageNet and few-shot meta-learning benchmarks. With neural
network models, our results indicate that Nesterov's Accelerated Gradient outperforms
other optimizers, particularly in larger network configurations. Additionally, our
research suggests that for smaller network models, the choice of optimization algorithm
has a minimal impact on performance.

Cross-domain recommendation is gaining significant attention in recent years as it tackles the challenges of cold-start and sparse ratings. Current approaches typically focus on a single target domain for recommendation. However, in practical scenarios, multiple target domains with various goods are often available, which can leverage each other's synergies to break the limitations of sparse data in individual domains. To address this, we propose the Multi-Sparse-Domain Collaborative Recommendation (MSDCCR) model, which considers user preferences across multiple sparse target domains simultaneously. To handle sparsity in each domain, we employ auto-encoders to reconstruct sparse target domain data. We then introduce an interaction module to capture the relationships between target domains and introduce cross-domain attention to integrate them. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that MSDCR outperforms existing cross-domain recommendation models in terms of accuracy.

Convex optimization issues, with linear constraints, can be complicated and hindered by the slowness of current solution methods. Exotic cones offer a potential solution by providing a more efficient approach, as they have well-studied properties that enable the use of closed-form solutions and reformulations to second-order cone problems. This reformulation allows for solving a diverse range of convex problems using established interior point methods. To expedite these solutions, we have developed custom code for computing exotic cones and integrated it with an existing library for second-order cone problems, resulting in a new solver called NPS. Our code has been applied to various problems, yielding up to an order of magnitude speedup in solution times for selected test cases.

The effectiveness of automated quality control in MRI analysis is heavily influenced by the appropriate selection and combination of criteria to identify faulty scans. Until now, there has been a lack of research on the optimal choice and integration of these features for a high-performance automated system. In this study, we aim to evaluate various types of automatic selection methods, including traditional machine learning algorithms and more recent techniques like attention-based models and neural architecture search. We developed and tested these models on a large dataset comprising both healthy and abnormal MRI scans, as well as artificially created outliers. The experimental results indicate that the use of automated quality control is essential in medical MRI analysis and that the best approach to identifying faulty scans involves a combination of multiple evaluation metrics. Furthermore, we found that the most effective automatic selection methods are those that prioritize samples with high variability and a high level of isolation. These models demonstrated superior performance compared to previous state-of-the-art algorithms in identifying abnormal scans and artificially created outliers.

To understand how private electric vehicles influence the recovery of power grids following outages, we developed a mathematical framework that incorporates decentralized decision-making in both transportation and energy systems. We utilized multi-agent optimization to model this process and overcame computational challenges through an efficient algorithm. Numerical analysis was performed using the Nonhomogeneous Spatial Aggregation method, demonstrating how private vehicles contribute to the restoration of electrical networks. We further illustrated our findings with specific case scenarios.

Intel's Optane DC Persistent Memory Module offers an cost-effective alternative to DRAM, maintaining DRAM-like performance while offering non-volatility.  Unlike DRAM, Optane retains stored data in the absence of power, enabling innovative applications such as system state preservation and system recovery. Moreover, Optane can be utilized in real-time scenarios where systems must remain operational during power outages.

This study investigates the feasibility of leveraging Optane DC Persistent Memory for system state preservation and recovery, presenting an application framework that leverages Optane's unique characteristics.  The proposed system, which utilizes Optane for data storage, can automatically recover from power failures, avoiding the need to restart the system and resuming the process from where it left off.

Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed system can achieve system recovery within 10 seconds, a performance that outperforms traditional operating system-based system recovery methods.  Moreover, the proposed system can also enable the design of fault-tolerant applications, such as a real-time stock application, with enhanced performance.  The results show that the proposed system can also recover the application state within 10 seconds, a performance that outperforms state-of-the-art distributed fault-tolerant recovery approaches.

The Motivation Dynamics framework, a concept explored in recent studies that applies bifurcations to model an autonomous agent's decision-making processes, is further developed to accommodate multiple autonomous entities in this paper. We demonstrate how the framework's capabilities can be expanded to capture persistent, cooperative behavior between agents meeting at specific locations, and through a combination of analytical and numerical methods, investigate the influence of additional motivation variables on this new dynamic.

This paper examines the structural, electronic, and magnetic characteristics of GdSn3, CmSn3, and the series GdxCm1-xSn3 using first-principles calculations. We find that GdSn3 and CmSn3 possess a AuCu3-type structure, while GdxCm1-xSn3 adopts a face-centered cubic structure. Our analysis shows that these compounds are metallic. The equilibrium lattice constants align closely with experimental data. By analyzing the density of states, we determine that both GdSn3 and CmSn3 are typical itinerant 4f metal semiconductors, whereas the series GdxCm1-xSn3 exhibits metallic behavior. Furthermore, our study of the phonon dispersion curves and elastic constants indicates the structural stability of these compounds. The calculated bulk modulus values are in line with experimental measurements. The projected density of states highlights the significant contribution of Gd 5d and 4f, Cm 5d and 4f states near the Fermi level, resulting in strong magnetism. The magnetic moments of GdSn3, CmSn3, and the series GdxCm1-xSn3 are predominantly influenced by 4f states. GdSn3 and CmSn3 display ferromagnetic properties, while the series GdxCm1-xSn3 exhibits antiferromagnetic ordering. The Curie temperatures of GdSn3 and CmSn3 are 175 K and

The paper analyzes the predictions of the bilepton model, specifically the MiM scheme, which involves a modified gauge group. The effective potential of Higgs fields is computed, along with constraints from gauge boson masses. Effective four-fermion interactions are derived from two Higgs triplets and two scalar bileptons, and their impact on muon antimuon scattering is studied.

The concept of ordered generating sequences (OGS) was initially expanded to non-abelian groups by S. M. Gagola in 1970. For any group G, there exists a finite set of generators such that every element within the group can be expressed uniquely as a sequence of powers of the generators or their inverses. If this generating set is taken from the set $\sigma$ of all ordered generating sequences of a group G, it has been proven that $\sigma$ forms a representation of the group as a quotient of the free monoid on a certain set, enabling analysis of the properties of the expanded group. Additionally, certain subsets of the free monoid that can represent a group were analyzed, with a focus on identifying the conditions under which the expanded group exhibits the Hopf property.

A new technique is proposed to use supernovae as weak lensing probes, taking advantage of the clustering of dark matter halos.  Our method relies on measuring small fluctuations in the magnitudes of Type Ia supernovae caused by dark matter's effect on their light.  By associating each supernova with its host galaxy and measuring the difference in magnitude between them, we can bypass the limitations of traditional lensing measurements, which are constrained by the resolution of our instruments.  We have developed a theoretical framework to model this approach and found that it can provide useful information about the distribution of dark matter halos, especially at intermediate distances.  We have also conducted simulations to test the approach and found that systematic effects, such as the color of the supernovae and the properties of their host galaxies, can be modeled and accounted for.  We have also found that the approach can be sensitive to the concentration of dark matter halos, which is an important parameter in cosmology.  We have also estimated the precision with which the approach can measure the concentration of these halos, which is around 10-20%.  This approach can be applied to existing and future surveys, such as the Dark Energy Survey and the Vera C. Rubin Observatory Legacy Survey of Space and Time.

These are lecture notes for a 6-hour mini-course on stochastic partial differential equations presented at the University of Oxford in April-May 2021. 

The main objective of these lecture notes is to provide an in-depth examination of the variational method for monotone and coercive stochastic partial differential equations. 

The necessary background on Hilbert space-based functional analysis, operator theory, and stochastic analysis has been recapitulated within the lecture notes. 

The accompanying video presentations are available at the following URL: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLyqQZ74l5c0jebQsQ4944444444444444.

The development of efficient and controllable quantum communication networks will rely heavily on discovering reliable methods to create stable interactions between photons and matter. In this context, we are investigating the T defect in silicon as a suitable platform for achieving reliable photon-spin connections. By performing ultrafast spectroscopy on a high-quality silicon sample, doped with phosphorus and exposed to a stress of uniaxial type, we discovered that the T defect exhibits distinct characteristics, including a large red-shift compared to donor atoms and a resonance that changes based on the direction of polarization. Furthermore, comparing the resonance of negative-charge and neutral T defects allows us to determine an electron attachment ionization energy of approximately 0.45 eV. Although research into the origin of the T defect has not yet produced conclusive results, we believe that it could be an effective candidate for a stable and controllable interaction point between photons and matter in doped silicon.

MRI technology utilizes radio waves to scan the human body and obtain precise, non-invasive diagnostic information. The success of MRI technology is partly attributed to advancements in computer hardware, specifically high-performance processors. This study presents an exploration of using Graph Processing Units (GPUs) to improve processor performance for real-time operation in MRI systems. A customized GPU-based solution is developed, featuring a Graph Tensor Decomposition (GTD) noise reduction technique to enhance signal quality. The notebook-based platform enables users to operate the system and obtain preliminary preview images. Furthermore, the GPU optimization led to a significant improvement in computational speed, resulting in nearly a tenfold increase in processing speed for real-time MRI applications.

In this research, we explore the properties of a novel algebraic variant of the degenerate Bernoulli polynomial $\tilde{\beta}_{k}(m,x)$, as well as its corresponding degenerate Bernoulli number. This investigation is grounded in an innovative algebraic framework for generating functions. Our analysis reveals that $\tilde{\beta}_{k}(m,x)$ possesses an intricate relationship with the degenerate Stirling number of the first kind, thereby illuminating its underlying mathematical structure.

The high activity levels of M dwarfs create a challenge in distinguishing between stellar activity and the signals of potential exoplanets. This is further complicated by the fact that these stars have large, complex magnetic activities. As a result, the stars' activities can mimic the stellar spots that are often used to detect exoplanets. This phenomenon can lead to the false identification of exoplanets or the misinterpretation of the stars' rotation periods. To address this issue, researchers are developing methods to quantify the stellar activity levels and understand their effects on the detection of exoplanets. This includes the use of activity indicators and machine learning algorithms to deconvolve the stellar activity signals. Ultimately, a precise measurement of the stars' radial velocities is necessary to differentiate between the stellar activity and the gravitational influence of exoplanets. This will allow for a more accurate detection of exoplanets around M dwarfs.

This research paper proposes Bidirectional Link Quality Estimation, an approach to estimate the transmission success rate between two nodes in a wireless sensor network.

In order to address energy constraints, a method is presented that allows nodes to operate in a sleep mode for extended periods.

Furthermore, a technique is developed to determine the necessary transmission attempts before sending data to active neighbor nodes, thereby reducing transmission power consumption.

Experiments conducted on real-world WSN testbeds demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed solutions.

The use of context in deep learning-based object detectors has evolved over the past decade, yet current methods lack a unified framework for leveraging hierarchical context. This study proposes a new framer for the detection system that can effectively utilise the inherent hierarchical context present in input images. Our proposed frame, based on a pyramid convolutional network, restructures 2D convolutions into a set of 2D and cross-layer connections that mimic the context present in the image pyramid. As a result, our method achieves a 4improvement in performance over current context-aware detectors while using half the computational resources. Furthermore, our framework is versatile and can be applied to various detection tasks, including multi-scale target identification, solid and non-solid target detection, and consistent performance across different levels of the pyramid.

The main objective of this paper is to investigate multiple solution possibilities for a specific Kirchhoff type elliptic system that contains quadratic and $p$-growth nonlinearities. By utilizing critical point theory and a minimax principle, we establish a multiplicity of solution outcome.

We examine the concentration behavior of convex functions under the influence of determinantal and binary determinantal measures. By analyzing this, we establish lower bound inequalities in the Ising and Bertrand's Paradox scenarios, tailored specifically for matrix-valued functions. Our research yields new strong Rayleigh inequality formulations for convex functions of a given rank, which can be decomposed into concentration inequalities for a variety of scalar functions. These inequalities for the isotropic case and their applications were previously demonstrated in a related study. Additionally, our findings relate to and complement concentration inequalities for a partial order under DRU log-concave measures, as explored in another paper. Our results also have implications for the partial hypercontractivity of matrix-valued functions under these measures.

Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic greater than two, and consider the ring of power series $R$ over the Witt vectors of $k$, expanded in variables $t_1, \dots, t_d$. The main aim of this study is to generalize classical Fontaine-Messing theory to a base ring of the form $R$. Notably, we establish theorems enabling the comparison of crystalline and \'etale cohomologies with torsion coefficients for smooth schemes $X$ over $R$.

This study explores the double longitudinal-spin asymmetry in semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering where hadron pairs' transverse momentum is not considered. Specifically, we investigate the cause of the cosine azimuthal asymmetry in hadron production, accounting for the connection between the helicity distribution $g_1$ and the twist-3 dihadron fragmentation function. Using a spectator model, we calculate the interference term between $s$-wave and $p$-wave and estimate this asymmetry at various experiments, including COMPASS, JLab 12 GeV, and the future EIC. Our analysis suggests that the cosine azimuthal asymmetry in SIDIS can serve as a key test for the dihadron fragmentation function.

We've established previously that the $\kappa$-deformation of relativistic special theory can be formalized through a star-product, and we now apply the Fock transformation to verify this, utilizing Moyal's approach. The transformation allows us to recover standard quantum mechanics from deformed versions, maintaining consistency with the positive unitarity requirements for the deformed S-matrix. The star-product derived from this transformation aligns with our earlier formulation based on deformed Poincaré symmetries, and it preservers the causality structure inherent in special relativity. Moreover, it leads to $ \kappa $-Minkowski spacetime as a one-sided module over the deformed algebra of coordinates, and it facilitates a straightforward derivation of the epimorphism responsible for recovering standard physics at the Planck scale.

Wilberd van der Kallen translated this 1951 thesis into English, originally written by T.A. Springer. Springer investigated the method of categorizing conjugacy classes within the symplectic group Sp_n(K), specifically focusing on fields K with a characteristic of not two. He developed two approaches using mathematical objects: bi-normalized rational canonical forms and Lagrangian equivalence classes of rational normal forms. Furthermore, he established the relationship between these two methods and characterized the set of elements in the same conjugacy class by identifying properties within a specific polynomial ring.
This paper presents a Wikipedia-based entity recommendation framework that utilizes an embedding approach and a graph-based method of automatic entity introduction.

A key challenge in kidney transplants with incompatible donors is a specific antibody issue that can shorten the transplant's lifespan. To address this, a policy called the STAR protocol was developed, but it's not entirely effective. Our innovative approach, which combines machine learning with medical data, aims to enhance prediction accuracy for this antibody problem. Specifically, we developed a predictive model using the STAR training dataset to anticipate the occurrence of Delayed Graft Function. This model outperformed the existing SFA prediction method, offering a more accurate and reliable solution to this complex medical issue.

Implicit copulas are the primary choice for analyzing dependencies in complex scenarios with multiple variables due to their flexibility in modeling dependencies and ease of calculation. This paper investigates a range of implicit copulas, including elliptical, skew t, multivariate Gumbel, t-series ARMA-GARCH, and factor copulas, by examining their definitions, marginal distributions, methods for generating data, and calculating likelihoods. Notably, we discover that some copulas, like elliptical and skew t, can be redefined in terms of mixture models, while others, like implicit factor copulas, are composites of copula mixtures and can be broken down into simpler components. This modular nature allows for the combination of various models to match the data's characteristics, and we explain how R packages can be utilized to compute likelihoods for these complex models.

The effectiveness of NLP applications heavily relies on a well-known assumption: words with similar distributions within a given corpus share similar meanings, and thus, their distribution patterns are also similar. This assumption serves as the foundation for the widely used neural bag-of-words models in NLP. These models, trained to minimize the negative sampling loss, implicitly construct a word representation that captures the distributional properties of the corpus. In this study, we investigate this assumption by analyzing a diverse range of texts, from Wikipedia articles to social media posts, and by plotting the 2D projections of the resulting embeddings using t-SNE. Our empirical findings confirm the validity of the assumption and reveal the following key properties of neural bag-of-words embeddings: (1) words with similar distributions tend to have similar meanings, (2) embedding training effectively captures the semantic structure of the target corpus, and (3) embeddings generated from different sub-corpora of the same corpus tend to be consistent with each other.

This article presents the SISO-OFDM and MISO-OFDM based IDET systems as alternatives to our previously proposed optimal wideband waveforming technique.
Two new suboptimal code designs are developed to enhance SISO-OFDM and MISO-OFDM IDET performance.
To achieve maximum code correlation under the least peak amplitude constraint, both methods first transform SISO-OFDM and MISO-OFDM ideality code design into traditional OFDM precoding issues,
then modify standard OFDM reception to meet ideality and quasi-ideality requirements.
We evaluate code performance in simulations that mimic wideband ideal code design conditions.

This research introduces a new method to model the interaction of fluids with changing phases, combining level-set and embedded boundary techniques. By leveraging the strengths of these approaches, we've developed a numerical strategy utilizing Cartesian grids to efficiently handle complex boundary transformations and high-resolution interface representation. This method enables a second-order conservative numerical scheme and has been effectively applied to solve various problems, including moving and deforming boundary problems in the context of Euler and Navier-Stokes equations.

Current versions of the Lambek Calculus used in computational linguistics are expanded upon using unary modalities to govern structural rules related to resource disposal. Initially, this provided a basic form of associativity, but it also created issues with ambiguity in parsing. In the context of human language, where sentence structure can be complex and ambiguous, this issue is particularly relevant. To address this problem, we have reinterpreted directional categorial grammar within the calculational framework of the Lambek Calculus by introducing a more advanced set of rules that include left and right contraction, left exchange, and a modalities expansion rule. This new approach allows us to derive intricate associations and swap left and right segments, and as a result, we have the capacity to parse and generate ambiguous sentences.

In multiagent learning environments, limited rationality typically results in Coarse Correlated Equilibria (CCE), a concept that allows for equilibria strategies based on individual knowledge. Conversely, Correlated Equilibria (CE) assumes that agents have comprehensive knowledge about all other agents' states. This paper argues that in learning settings, CCE is the more appropriate framework and proposes an algorithm to learn efficient CCEs in tabular concurrent games. The algorithm guarantees the discovery of a CCE within a specified number of steps and, under certain conditions, can identify a more optimal CCE. Moreover, it is demonstrated that the algorithm's current method for ensuring CCE validity can be refined, and in specific cases, the algorithm effectively approximates CE.

An analysis of a stochastic Susceptible-Infected model is conducted, where the model is based on a large population with potential for the fraction infected to remain non-zero in the limit as noise accumulates. For models above and at the threshold of the final fraction infected, distinct differences in behavior are found. For models above the threshold, the final fraction infected exhibits a non-uniform distribution, whereas for models at the threshold, it follows a Gamma distribution. Additionally, the long-term behavior of the susceptible model is found to differ based on whether it is above, at or below the threshold, resulting in various outcomes including non-exponential waiting times and the possibility of persistent susceptible populations.

In this research, we examine Cotton solitons within the context of almost Kenmotsu 3-$h$-manifolds. Initially, we establish the incompatibility of such solitons when the potential vector field is directly aligned with the Reeb vector field. Subsequently, assuming the potential vector field is perpendicular to the Reeb vector field, we derive the specific characteristics of the Reeb $\eta$-expansion and classify the reeb direction as being either lightlike or timelike. Finally, if the Reeb direction is confirmed to be spacelike, we demonstrate that the manifold is $\phi$-recurrent.

Integrating diverse datasets, stemming from data and theoretical sources, is a prerequisite for accurate fitting of Parton Distribution Functions (PDFs). While the statistical statistical combination of experimental data is a straightforward process, the incorporation of various cross-section predictions poses a more complex challenge. This complex process necessitates aligning differences in kinematic variables, combing finite and infinite momentum components consistently, and adjusting for distinct kinematic variables such as xQ^2. We outline the essential steps and critical aspects to consider when fitting PDFs to ensure the seamless integration of cross-sectional predictions.

To accelerate policy optimization in complex, dynamic systems with multiple influencing factors, reinforcement learning agents can effectively utilize past data. However, traditional experience replay methods require large datasets that are often unattainable in practical applications. A group of researchers recently proposed using smaller, secondary neural networks to store and share past observations with primary optimization models. Although these networks can provide valuable data, they eventually start propagating misleading information as they refine their data representations. To prevent this issue, experience replay models using neural networks typically become non-convergent. This research suggests employing parallel auxiliary data models that regularly reset and retrain on original real-time data. The proposed method guarantees optimal performance over time and consistently outperforms traditional policy optimization methods like PPO in simulated scenarios.

I'd like to introduce libcommute, a versatile C++17 template library called
`commute`, which is designed for efficient manipulation and simplification of
complex polynomial operators commonly used in the field of quantum many-body
theories.  By building upon the capabilities of Sophus and Eigen, libcommute
offers a host of specialized polynomial operator templates, including support
for second-quantized operators.  These operators can be automatically
simplified using a set of customizable "super-commutation" relations that
polynomial operators adhere to.  Additionally, libcommute provides the ability
to calculate both the equation of motion and the Heitman-Lippmann projection
limit.  By taking advantage of modern CPU instruction sets, this C++17
library delivers a versatile and user-friendly interface for the manipulation
and automatic simplification of polynomial operators in the field of quantum
many-body theories, ultimately leading to more efficient computations.

Recent experimental data obtained from angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy and scanning tunneling microscopy reveal the presence of a flat band in iron-based superconductors near the center of the Brillouin zone. To gain insight into this band, we performed a comprehensive analysis of multiple iron-based superconductors using a tight-binding model, accounting for the structural differences in their unit cells. Our results show that the band in question corresponds to a unique feature found in carbide-based superconductors, where it appears as an isolated low-energy band.
